title: (4.7-beta2) Imported .glb files using stale cached imported scene after reimport
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7-beta2, 4.7.2-stable
- Not reproducible in 4.6.3-stable

Didn't have time to do a full bisect

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable - Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS 26.04 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (ADL GT2) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-1240P (16 threads) - 15.32 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

Imported GLBs (and possibly other assets) use a stale cached imported scene even after automatic and manual reimports under certain conditions (described below).

NOTE: This does not occur when using .blend files directly, only with exported .glb/.gltf scenes.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/156b255d-ba5f-4331-997b-49bb9286e519

### Steps to reproduce

This is basically a description of the video above.

1. Open MRP and test.tscn.
2. Export the test cube .blend as a glb into the mrp resources folder.
3. Drag into the scene to ensure import is correct (optional).
4. Delete the instance you added in step 3 from test.tscn so no instance is open (this is important).
5. In Blender, make some noticeable change and re-export, overwriting the glb (in the video I just scaled on the x axis and applied the transformation).
6. Back in Godot, after automatic reimport finishes, drag the glb into the scene again. Somehow, the initial (unmodified) imported scene will be used instead of the newly modified glb.
7. Delete the instance you added in step 6.
8. Open the import settings by double clicking the glb file in the filesystem dock. You'll see the new (modified) scene as it should be. Click "Reimport".
9. Repeat step 6, and notice it is still using the stale (unmodified) imported scene even after manual reimport.
10. Even deleting the glb entirely, re-exporting from blender, and repeating step 6 will result in the same issue.
11. Now, *with the instance of the stale glb still open in the active scene*, repeat step 8. This time, reimport will work properly and the modified scene will appear correctly.

The only other way to make the reimport occur (if the imported scene isn't open/instanced anywhere) is to delete the .godot folder so the stale import doesn't exist anymore.

Issue is not present in 4.6.3-stable.


### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[import_caching_mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32868549/import_caching_mrp.zip)
